tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Balance in USD, current hourly spend, how long the balance lasts at that rate, and how many servers the account runs and may run.

tools.name: list_options
tools.description: What can be deployed right now: sizes (shared vCPU, dedicated CPU, NVIDIA GPU, bare metal) with vCPU, RAM, disk, included traffic, hourly and monthly price in USD, and the clouds (Vultr, DigitalOcean, Hetzner, Linode, OVHcloud for GPU) and city ids each one deploys in. Sorted by hourly price. Filter

tools.name: quote
tools.description: Price of a specific order: plan in a city (and optionally cloud, OS, count, hours). Returns the hourly price per server and in total, the cost for the given hours, the monthly price, and whether the current balance covers the first hour. Without a cloud it picks the cheapest one that deploys there.

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: One-click apps this account can deploy as the app of a new server: id, name, what it is, the minimum RAM and disk, and the clouds it deploys on. Each installs on Ubuntu 24.04 on first boot.

tools.name: list_servers
tools.description: Servers on the account (everything not destroyed): id, label, status, cloud, city, plan, IPv4, hourly price and a ready SSH command for running Linux servers.

tools.name: get_server
tools.description: One server by id: status (PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, STOPPED, ERROR and so on), IPv4, SSH command, plan, city, cloud and hourly price. Use it to follow a server that was still provisioning.

tools.name: create_server
tools.description: Creates 1 to 10 servers (default limit 3 per call) and waits up to about two minutes for ACTIVE, then returns ids, IPv4 and the SSH command. Spends money: billed per hour from the balance until the server is destroyed. Refused with the price if the total hourly price is above max_hourly_usd (default

tools.name: server_power
tools.description: reboot, stop (power off) or start a server by id. A stopped server keeps its IP and disk and is still billed per hour while it exists; destroying it ends billing.

tools.name: destroy_server
tools.description: Permanently deletes a server and its disk; billing stops in the hour it is destroyed. Needs confirm: true and the server's exact label. Without both it only describes what would be destroyed.

tools.name: recommend_plan
tools.description: Picks the cheapest sizes that fit a workload, across clouds and cities, from what can be deployed now. Describe the workload (e.g. "Minecraft for 12 players", "Llama 3.1 8B with Ollama", "WireGuard VPN for 5 people") and add numbers when known. Returns fitting options with hourly and monthly price,

tools.name: rename_server
tools.description: Changes a server's label (also renamed at the cloud). Latin letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, up to 64 characters.

tools.name: set_rdns
tools.description: Sets the reverse DNS (PTR) of a server's IPv4 to a hostname, for example mail.example.com. The hostname's A record must already point at the server's IP. Works on Vultr, Linode and Hetzner servers.

tools.name: get_bandwidth
tools.description: Outbound traffic a server used in the current billing period against the traffic its plan includes, in GB. Tracked for Vultr and Hetzner servers.

tools.name: reset_root_password
tools.description: Sets a new random root password on a running Linux server, without touching the disk, and returns it once. The password stays in the chat history: log in, add an SSH key and change it. Linux only.

tools.name: get_windows_password
tools.description: Returns the Administrator password of a Windows server for RDP. Secret: it stays in the chat history, so change it inside Windows after you log in.

tools.name: get_app_password
tools.description: Returns the admin login and password of a one-click app (for example WordPress or BTCPay) once it has finished installing. Secret: it stays in the chat history, so change it in the app.

tools.name: console_link
tools.description: A fresh web console session for a server (keyboard and screen, works without SSH). Returns a link when the cloud gives one, otherwise the dashboard page where the console opens. The link is a live session: anyone who has it can use the console, so do not share it.

tools.name: reinstall_server
tools.description: Reinstalls the server's OS in place: the disk is ERASED, the IP stays. Needs confirm: true and the server's exact label; without both it only describes what would happen. Linux: pass ssh_public_key; without it a new random root password is returned once and stays in the chat history. Windows gets a

tools.name: change_ip
tools.description: Moves a server to a new IPv4 address: it is snapshotted and recreated in the same city with the same disk contents, and the old address is released for good. Takes several minutes of downtime. Sets a new random root password, returned once (it stays in the chat history). Needs confirm: true and the

tools.name: list_backups
tools.description: Backups (disk snapshots) on the account, or of one server: id, label, status (PENDING, AVAILABLE, ERROR), city, cloud, size, when it was taken and until when it is kept (7 days).

tools.name: create_backup
tools.description: Takes a snapshot of a server's whole disk, at no extra charge, kept for 7 days. Works on Vultr cloud servers that are running or stopped. Takes a few minutes; the backup then shows status AVAILABLE.

tools.name: restore_backup
tools.description: Creates a NEW server from a backup in the backup's city and cloud, billed per hour like any server. Optionally on a bigger plan. Needs confirm: true; without it returns the price. Refused with the price if it costs more than max_hourly_usd (default $1). Sets a new random root password, returned once

tools.name: delete_backup
tools.description: Permanently deletes a backup. Needs confirm: true and the backup's exact label; without both it only describes what would be deleted.

tools.name: list_load_balancers
tools.description: Load balancers on the account: id, label, status, city, public IPv4, forwarding rules, backend servers and hourly price.

tools.name: create_load_balancer
tools.description: Creates a managed load balancer in a city in front of your servers there, $0.0247/hour ($18.00/month), billed per hour from the balance until it is deleted. Spends money. Backends are ACTIVE vultr or hetzner servers in that city, all on one cloud. Refused with the price if it is above max_hourly_usd

tools.name: set_load_balancer_backends
tools.description: Replaces the set of servers behind a load balancer (pass the full new list; an empty list removes all). Servers must be ACTIVE, in the load balancer's city and on its cloud.

tools.name: delete_load_balancer
tools.description: Deletes a load balancer and its public IP; the servers behind it keep running. Billing for it stops in the hour it is deleted. Needs confirm: true and the exact label; without both it only describes what would be deleted.

tools.name: billing_history
tools.description: Recent movements of the balance (newest first, up to 50): top-ups, hourly charges, refunds, referral credits, with the balance after each.

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description: Invoices issued for credited crypto top-ups: number, date and amount. The documents open from the Profile page of the dashboard (card payments get a receipt from the card processor instead).

tools.name: list_deposits
tools.description: Recent top-ups (open and credited, up to 20): amount to pay, amount credited, method, status (PENDING, CREDITED), payment link of open ones and when they expire.

tools.name: request_server_limit
tools.description: Asks for a higher limit on how many servers the account may run at once. Often approved on the spot depending on the account's top-up history; otherwise the team reviews it. One open request at a time.

tools.name: list_payment_methods
tools.description: How the balance can be topped up: crypto coins and networks (with their method codes) and the minimum amount for each, and card if offered to this account.

tools.name: top_up
tools.description: Creates a payment request for the balance and returns where to pay: a payment link, or an address with the exact amount and network. Nothing is charged until the user pays it. Without sanctions_confirmed the tool creates nothing and returns the sanctions statement that the user confirms. method is a

tools.name: support_read
tools.description: The latest messages of this account's own support chat with NoctHost (oldest first): what the user wrote, replies from the support AI assistant and from the team. Marks replies as read.

tools.name: support_send
tools.description: Sends a message to NoctHost support in this account's own chat, on the user's behalf; the team sees it marked as sent by an AI assistant. At most 5 messages per hour per key. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_windows_password, get_app_password, request_server_limit, support_read · Private data: list_servers, get_server, create_server, set_rdns, reset_root_password, get_windows_password, get_app_password, console_link, reinstall_server, change_ip, restore_backup, list_invoices · Public sink: console_link, support_send · Destructive: get_account, destroy_server, reset_root_password, delete_backup, delete_load_balancer, request_server_limit.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_windows_password, get_app_password, request_server_limit, support_read · Private data: list_servers, get_server, create_server, set_rdns, reset_root_password, get_windows_password, get_app_password, console_link, reinstall_server, change_ip, restore_backup, list_invoices · Public sink: console_link, support_send · Destructive: get_account, destroy_server, reset_root_password, delete_backup, delete_load_balancer, request_server_limit

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
